subject: Energy
title: Energy Access and Gender
description: Learn Energy Access and Gender in one minute.

hook.text: Women and girls bear the greatest burden of energy poverty—spending hours daily collecting firewood and cooking.

buildup.text: In sub-Saharan Africa, women spend 1–4 hours daily gathering fuel—time that could be used for school or work.

discovery.text: Electricity enables women's economic participation—lighting lets small businesses operate after dark, boosting income.

twist.text: Despite bearing the burden, women hold only 22% of energy jobs—vastly underrepresented in energy decisions.

climax.text: Gender-inclusive energy programs show better outcomes—products designed with women's input see higher adoption rates.

punchline.text: Energy poverty hits women hardest—solutions must center them.

quiz.question: How much time do women in sub-Saharan Africa spend gathering fuel daily?
